questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the events that directly triggers a sharing recalculation?
options: A role is moved within the role hierarchy
A public group's membership changes
A user updates a free-text field on a record they own
A sharing rule is created, edited, or deleted
questions.explain: Editing an ordinary field on an owned record doesn't change any sharing input; recalculation is driven by role, territory, group-membership, and sharing-rule changes.

questions.q: Where can an admin see which specific changes have historically triggered sharing recalculations?
options: Setup Audit Trail
The Recycle Bin
The object's page layout editor
Data Loader's error log
questions.explain: Setup Audit Trail logs exactly which changes (and who made them) triggered recalculation, useful for diagnosing a pattern of repeated recalculation pain.

questions.q: What does Resume Sharing Calculations actually do after a batch of deferred changes?
options: It reverts all changes made while deferral was active
It permanently disables future sharing recalculation for the org
It converts all sharing rules into Apex managed sharing
It runs one recalculation reflecting the net effect of the whole batch, instead of one per change
questions.explain: Resume Sharing Calculations triggers a single, consolidated recalculation covering everything done during deferral, rather than recalculating after every intermediate step.

questions.q: What is the specific risk an architect takes on during a deferred window?
options: The org's OWD values are temporarily reset to Public Read/Write
All sharing rules are permanently deleted
Sharing access may not reflect the in-progress role/territory/group changes until Resume Sharing Calculations runs
Users lose the ability to log in until the window closes
questions.explain: During deferral the sharing table still reflects the pre-deferral state for the affected changes, so real users' actual access can be temporarily out of sync with the intended new structure.

questions.q: Per this lesson's recommended pattern, when should Defer Sharing Calculations be used?
options: Only as an emergency measure after a recalculation job has already been running for hours
As a planned step for any deliberate batch of role, territory, or group-membership changes, ideally during a maintenance window
Automatically, on every single sharing rule edit regardless of scale
Never, since it is deprecated functionality
questions.explain: The lesson frames deferral as a deliberate, planned part of a bulk hierarchy/territory/group change — scheduled and verified, not a reactive fix for an incident already in progress.
